title: Statement Written by Police in Cornell Assault Case Omitted Her Claim She Was Raped
summary: Documents obtained by The New York Times show that the campus police at Cornell University sent a condensed statement to a prosecutor, who then declined to bring charges.

summary: Their accounts, detailed in hundreds of pages of investigative files obtained by The New York Times, were disjointed. All the men denied any wrongdoing.

summary: The woman known as “Jane Doe” was initially embarrassed about what happened at a fraternity party in 2024, but soon concluded: “I was assaulted.”

title: What Did Christa Pike Do? What to Know About the Botched Tennessee Execution.
summary: Ms. Pike, 50, survived two doses of a lethal injection in Tennessee. She was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of a classmate.

title: As Mortgage Rates Hit Highest Level Since 2023, Buyers Look at ARMs
summary: The average 30-year, fixed-rate home loan rose to 7.28 percent, up from 6.34 percent a year ago. More buyers are now turning to adjustable-rate mortgages.

title: U.S. Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002
summary: The factors pushing up yields, including the war in Iran and high government debt levels, are unlikely to dissipate soon.

title: Trump’s Threat to Ban Diesel Exports Sets Off Global Alarms
summary: A reduction in refineries has already driven the price of diesel to record highs, threatening economies. An U.S. export ban would be “tremendous shock and blow.”

title: A Bloody Attack on a FlyDubai Plane Headed to Israel, and a Terrifying Plunge
summary: “I don’t deserve to die like this,” said one passenger on Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The motive of the cockpit stabbing remains unknown, officials said.

title: Supreme Court, Taking On Trump Immigration Agenda, Will Review Migrant Detention Policy
summary: The administration’s policy of detaining immigrants who crossed the border illegally years ago and holding them without a bond hearing has divided lower courts.

title: The Supreme Court’s Summer Break Vanishes, Erased by Emergencies
summary: “Our summers used to actually be summers,” one justice lamented.

summary: After decades of potlucks and paddle-boarding on Maine’s midcoast, rising anger and protests have left the Supreme Court’s chief justice more isolated than ever.

summary: Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.

summary: Allies of Gina Hinojosa want a Democratic group to support her bid for Texas governor — putting pressure on its chairman, Gov. Andy Beshear of Kentucky, who is weighing a run for president.

summary: Many think artificial intelligence companies should be held liable for their runaway technology. But legal scholars say applying existing law could be messy

summary: For an upcoming project, we’re looking for your memories of going door to door in apartment buildings.
